transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi. Um, thanks for seeing me. I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... I guess I came in because I've been having a little trouble sleeping lately. Well, I guess I barely sleep right anymore, to be honest. 

I'll just lie there in bed, and... I don't know, I keep hearing the rain, or I start thinking about, um... the bluff giving way. And then when I actually do manage to pass out, I keep waking up all sweaty from these dreams. It's mostly just frustrating because I show up to my shift at the call center feeling like I never even slept at all. 

Is that... I mean, is that a normal reason to come see you? I just really want to get back to doing a good job at work, you know?
Can you describe the dreams you're having when you wake up sweaty? Are they related to a specific event or more general worries?

Um, yeah, they are... I guess they are tied to a specific event. I hope it's okay if I don't go into all the details right this second, I just... I feel a little silly making a big deal out of it. But I had a bit of an accident on a trail a while back. 

Actually, it's not even just the dreams, if I'm being completely honest. Is it normal if it happens when you're awake, too? Because sometimes, um, stuff just pops in my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll be at work, and suddenly I swear I hear the sound of rocks sliding, or I'll get this weird feeling like my leg is stuck under me again. Just for a minute, it feels like I'm right back on that trail instead of sitting at my desk with my headset on. 

I always snap out of it, though! I try really hard not to let it affect my customer calls, I promise. I hope that makes sense... am I answering your question okay?
Since the accident on the trail, have you noticed that you often feel upset or experience negative emotions like fear, anger, or sadness when reminded of what happened?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try not to dwell on it too much, you know? I wouldn't say I get super upset or angry or anything like that. Maybe a little... I don't know, a little on edge sometimes if I see a picture of a hike or something, but it's nothing crazy. I'm usually pretty good at just pushing it aside and focusing on whatever I'm supposed to be doing. I don't want to be one of those people who complains all the time. I'm doing okay, really. Is that... does that sound like the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm overreacting or anything.
Since the accident, have you found yourself avoiding places, people, or thoughts that remind you of what happened?

Um, well... I guess I have changed my routine just a little bit. It's not a huge deal, I promise, but... I don't really go near the coast trails anymore. And, um, I feel kind of bad about this, but I've been dodging texts from my old hiking buddies. 

I just... even just the thought of talking to them about going back out there, it makes my chest feel all tight. I don't want to bring them down or ruin their fun, you know? So it's just easier to kinda stay away from it all for now. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad friend or anything. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing to get back on track. Does that make sense?
Since the accident, have you found yourself feeling persistently fearful, sad, or angry — even if it’s not intense or constant?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything, but... yeah, under the surface, I think I've been feeling kind of scared most days. And, um, embarrassed, if I'm being totally honest. 

It's just... I feel like everyone can tell I messed up out there, you know? Like they look at me and know I'm not as tough as I used to act. But I really try to keep a smile on at work and not let it show. I don't want to be a downer for anyone else. Is it normal to feel kind of... ashamed like that? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Since the accident, have you found yourself being more alert than usual, like you're always on the lookout for danger, or have you been startled more easily by things like loud noises?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm jumping at shadows or anything like that. I'm pretty relaxed most of the time, honestly. 

I guess... I mean, maybe if someone drops something heavy at work, I might flinch a little? But that's just a normal reaction, right? Anyone would do that. I definitely don't want you to think I'm walking around paranoid or completely on edge all day. I'm still doing my job and handling things fine. I'm not overreacting to stuff, I promise. Does that sound like a good answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Since the accident, have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities?

Um, well... no, I don't think so. I'm still trying to keep busy, you know? 

I mean, I haven't really been doing much on the weekends lately, just kind of hanging around the apartment. But that's mostly just because work has been a little tiring, not because I don't care about stuff anymore. I still like watching movies and playing video games when I have the energy. I definitely haven't given up on everything or anything like that. I'm trying my best to stay positive and keep things normal. Is that... is that okay? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get better.
Since the accident, have you noticed that you don’t feel as much joy or interest in the good things in life, like the way you used to?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still laugh at jokes and, you know, enjoy a good meal and stuff like that. 

I guess... maybe I haven't been quite as excited about things as I used to be? But I think that's just because I've been a little tired, like I said. It's not like I'm totally numb or anything. I still appreciate the good things, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself and ignoring all the positive stuff in my life. I'm really trying to focus on the good. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for.
Since the accident, have you found yourself feeling detached from other people or feeling numb in your relationships with them?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still talk to my friends and my family, and everything's pretty much the same with them. 

I guess... well, maybe I haven't been reaching out to hang out as much as I used to? But that's just because I don't want to bring anyone down or be a burden, you know? It's not that I don't care about them or feel disconnected. I definitely still love my family and care about my friends a lot. I'm not pushing anyone away or anything like that, I promise. I just... I want to make sure I'm being a good friend and not making things hard for them. Is that the right way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
Since the accident, have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for what happened, even if you know it wasn’t entirely your fault?

Um, well... I mean, I know it wasn't like, *all* my fault. I know that logically. 

But I guess sometimes I do kind of beat myself up a little bit. Just, you know, thinking I was maybe a bit stupid or careless for being out there alone in the first place. I shouldn't have put myself in that situation. And now... I don't know, it just feels like if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad is going to happen again. Like I have to be super careful all the time now so I don't make another dumb mistake. 

But I'm trying not to dwell on it too much, I really am! I know I need to move past it and not just sit around blaming myself. I'm trying to be more responsible now. Is it normal to feel a little bit like that? I just hope I'm not, you know, overreacting or handling this the wrong way.
Since the accident, have you noticed that you often feel afraid, sad, or upset, even if it's not all the time or very intense?

Um, I wouldn't say I'm always sad or anything like that. I try to keep a smile on, you know? Especially at work, dealing with customers and all that. 

But... I guess under the surface, yeah, maybe a little bit. Most days I do feel kind of... scared, I guess. And embarrassed. It just feels like everyone can tell I messed up, like they look at me and know I'm not as tough as I used to act. I try really hard to hide it, though, so it doesn't bother anyone else. I don't want people thinking I'm weak or anything. I'm still doing my job and everything, I promise. It's just hard to shake that feeling sometimes. Do you think that's okay? Like, is it alright that I'm feeling that way as long as I'm still trying my best?
Would you say that you feel fearful, sad, or upset on most days since the accident, even if those feelings aren't very strong or don't last all day?

Yeah, um, like I was just saying a second ago... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it is most days. I really try to push it down so I can do my job and be normal for the customers, but yeah. 

That scared feeling... and just feeling so embarrassed, like everyone knows I messed up and I'm not actually as tough as I try to act... it's pretty much always there right under the surface. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or feeling sorry for myself, I promise. I really am trying to keep a good attitude and not let it ruin my day. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just don't want you to think I'm not trying.
